body: This is because it uses the QuarkusTest annotation to turn test classes into beans.

Ok but can we fix it or at least provides a workaround? 

Using those annotations is the only way to ordering test extensions. So it is very important in order Quarkus to play well inside the Junit 5 ecosystem

We can fix, we would need to use Jandex index that we already have for
QuarkusTestResource to look for @RegisterExtension and @ExtendWith, and use
that to explicitly figure out which test classes are beans. You should be
able to work around this for now by putting a CDI scope on the test class.

On Sun, 16 Feb 2020 at 22:02, Loïc Mathieu <notifications@github.com> wrote:

@stuartwdouglas thanks, the workaround works! I annotated my class with `@Singleton` and it works.

Regarding a fix, I don't understand why you need Jandex, you can retrieve easily the test class inside an extension (via `extensionContext.getRequiredTestClass();`) and register it in CDI ...
QuarkusTest only starts Quarkus once for all tests, so we need to know all the test classes at the start.
